properties.text: A stopped state always applies the brakes, cuts the implement and zeroes the speed limit.
A pressed e-stop (machine or remote) gives an emergency stop in the same cycle.
An emergency stop is never cleared without a new supervisor reset (no automatic restart).
A violated front protective field of the selected set stops the machine in the same cycle, unless the front field is in supervised teleop recovery.
Same for the rear protective field (reversing, or at standstill).
Same for the side fields while the machine moves.
A scanner fault stops the machine.
While the warning hold is active the speed limit is at most the warning speed.
The commanded speed limit never exceeds the speed the scanners can protect.
Whenever the brakes are released on a travel field set, the measured speed is within what that set's protective field can stop from.
Loss of the remote supervision heartbeat (> 0.5 s) in AUTO or TELEOP stops the machine.
A stale autonomy command (> 0.2 s) in AUTO or TELEOP stops the machine.
In AUTO with a valid safety position outside the operating area, the machine stops.
In AUTO, a safety position invalid for more than 2 s stops the machine.
The two speed channels disagreeing by more than 0.3 m/s for more than 0.2 s stops the machine.
A stop is only ever cleared at standstill.
Without a supervisor reset, only self-clearing causes (fields, truck door) restart automatically.
The dig field set (front field muted) is only active when requested, inside the dig zone, with a valid position and at no more than the dig speed plus tolerance.
Muting held for more than 25 s stops the machine.
The implement (boom, bucket) is never enabled during recovery.
During recovery from a front stop, moving forward stops the machine; from a rear stop, reversing stops it.
During recovery from a side stop, an occupied contact band stops the machine (outside the access-controlled zones).
Recovery exists only in TELEOP.
While recovering with the brakes released, the speed limit is creep speed (0.5 m/s, 0.3 m/s for a side stop).
Every transition into a stop and every reset is written to the safety log.

Outside the dig zone, anyone between the front tyres and the bucket (near field, any boom position) or under the raised bucket (far field, except beside a docked truck) stops travel and holds the boom, unless backing away in recovery.
While reversing, anyone beside the front frame stops the machine (outside the dig zone and a docked truck), unless backing away from a side stop in recovery.
During recovery from an under-bucket stop, moving forward stops the machine, and the boom stays held.
The dock field set is never active while the truck's cab door is open.
The cab door opening while docking in the dock zone stops the machine.
